correctness.rationale: The expected seed stock follows from integrating constant post-maturity seed production against independent exponential viability loss. Fubini/layer-cake yields \(\mathbb E[B(\min(F,T))]\) as an exponential integral and \(\mathbb E[\min(F,T)]=(1-e^{-\mu T})/\mu\). The derivative numerator \(Q\) has a single turning point at \(\frac{(\mu+\delta)m}{\delta}\), is initially positive and tends to minus infinity, so \(J\) has exactly one finite global maximum; the explicit bracket follows by rearrangement. At the root \(g_T=-\delta\ell<0\), \(H\) is strictly increasing and negative, so \(g_\mu>0\), \(g_\delta<0\), and \(g_m>0\); implicit differentiation proves all comparative statics. Boundary and asymptotic formulas follow by direct limit and bracket. All positive parameters are quantified, not inferred from sampling. The standalone independent formula and deterministic checker returned 91,091 passing checks; finite tests do not certify continuous-domain proof.

value.rationale: Fire-regime choices for serotinous plants must balance immaturity risk and the aging loss of viable canopy-stored seeds. The exact policy reveals a mathematically sharp and potentially surprising direction: increasing competing wildfire hazard raises the unique idealized elective-fire deadline, despite greater premature-fire frequency; viability decay reverses this effect. The result also separates the two necessary mechanisms (maturation and viability loss) from their degenerate limits and gives an explicit deadline bracket and measurable benchmark. This is not merely the generic renewal-reward formula. Its limits prevent treating the proxy as a demographic or management recommendation.
